## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial gallery and one-click launch in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the product-code half of the curated getting-started
tutorial gallery: a Dashboard surface where users browse curated tutorials and
launch one into their own project with a single action. Launching a notebook
tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook
loaded; launching a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline into the user's
project. This epic delivers the gallery UI and the launch mechanics; the
curated tutorial content and its packaging format are delivered by separate
work streams.

## Scope

- A tutorial gallery section in the Dashboard listing the curated tutorials
  with their metadata (title, journey, description) as read from the tutorial
  packaging format.
- One-click launch of a notebook tutorial: creating/opening a workbench in
  the user's selected project with the tutorial's notebook content, using the
  pinned image recorded in the tutorial packaging.
- One-click launch of a pipeline tutorial: importing the tutorial's pipeline
  into the user's project.
- Gallery behavior when the tutorial catalog is empty or a tutorial fails
  validation (surfaced clearly to the user rather than a broken launch).
- Incidental UI text and in-product guidance for the gallery surface that
  falls out of this change (no standalone documentation work).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Dashboard shows a tutorial gallery listing the curated tutorials with
  their packaged metadata.
- From the gallery, a user can launch a notebook tutorial into their own
  project with a single action, resulting in a workbench running the
  tutorial's notebook with the pinned image specified by the tutorial
  packaging.
- From the gallery, a user can launch a pipeline tutorial into their own
  project with a single action, resulting in the pipeline imported into the
  project.
- The gallery correctly renders and launches only tutorials that pass their
  packaged validation status; invalid or missing tutorials are surfaced
  without breaking the gallery.
- Gallery and launch flows work for a user scoped to a single project via
  OpenShift RBAC (no cluster-level permissions required).

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Full — the tutorial gallery and one-click launch into the user's project (workbench with notebook, or pipeline import). |

# Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format — the shared contract that
makes curated tutorials versioned and testable independently of Dashboard
releases. The format specifies tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a
validation manifest. It is the framework the Dashboard gallery's launch
mechanics build against and that every curated tutorial is packaged,
versioned, and validated with. Defining it once here avoids three consumer
work streams each inventing their own packaging.

## Scope

- A written specification of the tutorial packaging format covering:
  - tutorial metadata (identity, journey, display information, version);
  - pinned image references for tutorial execution;
  - a validation manifest describing how a tutorial is tested against a
    target platform release.
- A validation mechanism that executes the validation manifest for a packaged
  tutorial and produces a pass/fail result against a target release.
- Versioning rules for packaged tutorials, so a tutorial can be updated and
    re-validated without a Dashboard release.
- Agreement on the format with the teams that consume it (Dashboard launch
  mechanics, notebook tutorial authoring, pipeline tutorial authoring) as
  part of normal design review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines tutorial metadata, pinned image
  references, and the validation manifest, and is reviewed by all three
  consuming work streams.
- A tutorial packaged per the format carries a version and can be re-versioned
  without any Dashboard release.
- Running the validation mechanism against a packaged tutorial produces a
  deterministic pass/fail result against a target platform release.
- Each consuming work stream — the Dashboard gallery's launch mechanics, the
  notebook tutorial authoring stream, and the pipeline tutorial authoring
  stream — confirms in writing at format sign-off that the format as
  specified meets its needs (one recorded sign-off per work stream); needs
  discovered after sign-off are met through the format's versioning rules
  rather than mid-stream format changes.

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-3 | P1 | Full — the packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) making tutorials versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. Epic priority is P0 by inheritance: this format directly enables the P0 gallery (HLR-1) and the P0 curated tutorials (HLR-2). |

# Curated notebook tutorial suite

## Description

This epic authors the notebook-based half of the six curated getting-started
tutorials: the workbench-centric journeys — first workbench, data prep, first
training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is a
maintained, tested notebook packaged per the tutorial packaging format, so it
can be launched from the Dashboard gallery and validated against the current
release independently of Dashboard releases. This is authored content, not
product code: it requires tutorial-writing and domain review rather than a
feature-code review cycle.

## Scope

- Five curated notebook tutorials covering: first workbench, data prep, first
  training run, first deployment, and first RAG app.
- Each tutorial packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest) and versioned.
- Each tutorial validated end-to-end against the current platform release via
  its validation manifest, and re-validated on release updates.
- Tutorial content kept aligned with the current release (maintained, not
  one-shot authoring).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist, one per journey: first workbench, data prep,
  first training run, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  a pinned image, and a validation manifest.
- Each tutorial's validation manifest passes against the current platform
  release.
- Each tutorial runs end-to-end from a fresh workbench launched with its
  pinned image, without manual fix-up steps.
- Each tutorial is launchable from the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard as
  packaged, with the launchability check run in the same release once the
  Dashboard tutorial gallery capability lands; independently of that check,
  each tutorial is verified end-to-end via its validation manifest.

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-2 | P0 | Partial (with the pipeline tutorial work stream) — the five workbench-centric journeys of the six curated tutorials, each tested against the current release. |

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for the tutorial gallery:
how to use the gallery (browsing and launching tutorials) and the
contribution process for new tutorials (how a tutorial is packaged, validated,
and submitted for inclusion). It follows the Red Hat docs content process and
is written after the implementation work it describes has settled, so the
documented behavior matches what shipped.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to be authored inside this epic):

- Using the tutorial gallery: what it is, browsing the curated tutorials,
  launching a notebook tutorial into a workbench, launching a pipeline
  tutorial into a project, and what the pinned images mean for the user.
- Contributing a new tutorial: the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest), how validation against a target
  release works, versioning expectations, and the submission/review path for
  new curated tutorials (documentation only — no submission tooling this
  release, per the strategy's out-of-scope statement).
- Cross-references from the getting-started/onboarding documentation into the
  gallery topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery,
  including launching notebook and pipeline tutorials.
- A published documentation topic covers the contribution process for new
  tutorials, including packaging, validation, and the review path.
- Both topics are technically reviewed against the implemented gallery,
  packaging format, and shipped tutorials (reviewed by or with the
  implementing teams), with discrepancies resolved before publication.
- The documentation contains no steps that fail against the shipped release.

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-4 | P2 | Full — documentation covering use of the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority Major → P1), not inheritance. |

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

Triage: neither Step 0 check fires. The strategy is not below-threshold — it
spans four components and, by its own problem statement, three architecturally
distinct work streams (product code for the gallery and launch mechanics,
authored tutorial content, and documentation) with different owners and review
processes. It is not docs-only — HLR-1/HLR-2/HLR-3 require product code and
authored content. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Component | Team | Priority | implementation_type |
|----|-------|------|-----------|------|----------|---------------------|
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Tutorial gallery and one-click launch in the Dashboard | Implementation | Dashboard | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 | — |

- The strategy states three kinds of work with different owners and review
  processes. The Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics are product code
  (RHOAI Dashboard). The tutorial packaging format is a shared contract that
  the gallery code and both tutorial-content streams build against, so it is
